source_row.item_data_json: {"options":{"A":"Avoid every nonantibiotic sulfonamide automatically, because all sulfonamide-containing drugs share allergy epitopes.","B":"Ignore the allergy label entirely, because the details and severity of a prior sulfonamide reaction never affect care.","C":"Assume any medication containing sulfur will cross-react, because elemental sulfur determines sulfonamide allergy risk in practice.","D":"Clarify the culprit drug and reaction; sulfonamide-antibiotic allergy does not imply broad cross-reactivity with nonantibiotics."}}
source_row.rationale: A sulfonamide-antibiotic allergy should be characterized by culprit and reaction. It does not justify assuming universal immunologic cross-reactivity with all nonantibiotic sulfonamides, though each proposed drug must still be assessed on its own risks.
source_row.source_detail: Sulfonamide allergy guidance: structural determinants of sulfonamide antimicrobial allergy differ from nonantimicrobial sulfonamides; broad allergic cross-reactivity is not supported, while history and specific drug/reaction remain important. 2022 Drug Allergy Practice Parameter Update; current parameter page rechecked 2026-08-15. Reviewed 2026-08-15.
source_row.source_name: AAAAI/ACAAI — 2022 Drug Allergy Practice Parameter Update
source_row.stem: A client reports a prior immediate allergy to a sulfonamide antibiotic. Another sulfonamide-containing medication is being considered. Which nursing interpretation is most accurate?
